paragraphs: Your posting describes the gap I have spent the last year standing in: engineers with good ideas on one side, a digital landscape that has to stay scalable on the other, and someone in the middle deciding what becomes a reusable module and what stays inside the discipline. I came into Python and automation from mechanical engineering, and the Lego-blocks framing is exactly how I have been building.

At Corominas Consulting I owned the automation layer across a portfolio of roughly 85 client systems. The core is a config-driven Python engine where behaviour lives in configuration rather than code branches, callable by a person or an orchestrator. In front of the generated output sits a deterministic checker written against the artefact rather than the generator, so changing the model does not invalidate it, with 715 assertion calls across 33 test scripts behind it. The part closest to your flywheel is the generation layer: four Python generators emit and maintain 26 workflow definitions totalling 490 nodes, reading templates from the real source modules at build time so orchestrator and package cannot drift. Onboarding a new instance became one command instead of a hand-edit of an eighteen-node canvas.

The enablement half is the part I enjoy. I co-owned a repository with a domain lead who owned the subject matter while I built the automation that runs his work, then built automation inside his components so each self-encapsulates and the outer pipeline consumes it as a single unit. Around that I wrote a readiness script that answers mechanically whether an instance is safe to switch on, and contract tests that fail when a rule gets traded away. I am also good at the failure mode that looks like success: a run cap applied to the wrong side of a filter left instances producing zero output forever with the log green.

On the future-ready side, SceneAgent turns video, photos, point clouds, BIM or a splat into a semantically queryable scene, with a LangGraph agent reaching it through MCP tools and pgvector behind it, so retrieval over structured expertise is familiar ground.
